**8B.2 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

Overall read: **yes, partly and concretely**. Srettha translated his 2024 program into visible **cabinet actions, named appointments, flagship policy moves, formal diplomatic positions, and some institutional/legal steps**. The weak point is that implementation often looked **ungainly, delayed, or fiscally contested**, and I found **little direct evidence of a full budgetary or enforcement architecture** beyond a few cases.

**Accepted Claims**
- **`Thailand's cabinet approves 135 billion digital-wallet handout`** | **Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-04-23** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailands-cabinet-approves-135-billion-digital-wallet-handout-3390007) | Cabinet approved the flagship 500 billion baht digital-wallet plan, showing Srettha turned his broad campaign promise into a concrete policy priority with a clear distribution mechanism. It is the clearest evidence of program-to-policy translation, even though it was fiscally controversial.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- **`Thailand’s flagship 14 billion handout`** | **Reuters via Yahoo News** | **2024-08-01** | [URL](https://www.yahoo.com/news/thailands-flagship-14-billion-handout-072635149.html) | Reuters reported registration snags, delayed launch timing, and criticism from economists and former central bankers. This shows that Srettha did move from slogan to implementation, but the execution side was weak and not yet stabilized.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`

- **`Thai PM says digital wallet scheme will spur jobs and manufacturing`** | **Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-07-11** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-pm-says-digital-wallet-scheme-will-spur-jobs-and-manufacturing-3514879) | After criticism, Srettha publicly reframed the handout as a jobs-and-manufacturing stimulus. That is concrete evidence of a policy narrative and a stated implementation rationale, though it also shows late rhetorical repositioning rather than a clean rollout plan.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`

- **`Thai ex-executive Pichai named finance minister, faces growth challenge`** | **Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-04-28** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thai-exexecutive-pichai-named-finance-minister-faces-growth-challenge-3401984) | Srettha appointed Pichai Chunhavajira, a former SET chair and Bank of Thailand board member, as finance minister and deputy PM. This is strong evidence that he translated his economic program into a technocratic appointment at the funding and macro-management level.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- **`Thailand Board of Investment` outreach to Australia** | **Public Relations Department, Kingdom of Thailand** | **2024-03-06** | [URL](https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/2078/iid/266801) | Srettha used formal policy channels to promote trade, investment, tourism, technology, innovation, and FTA improvement. This is concrete execution through an existing investment institution rather than only rhetoric.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- **`Thailand-Sri Lanka sign free trade agreement`** | **Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-02-03** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailand-sri-lanka-sign-free-trade-agreement-3291876) | Srettha signed an FTA covering goods, investment, customs procedures, and intellectual property. That is a concrete policy instrument, not just a stated goal, and it shows translation into legal-commercial architecture.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- **`Thailand working relentlessly to solve Myanmar crisis`** | **Bangkok Post, reporting Bloomberg News** | **2024-05-24** | [URL](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2798697/thailand-working-relentlessly-to-solve-myanmar-crisis-srettha) | Srettha framed the Myanmar response as reducing violence and spillover risk. This is evidence of a concrete foreign-policy priority being operationalized through crisis management, not just described abstractly.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`

- **`ASEAN foreign ministers' statement on Myanmar`** | **Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand** | **2024-04-18** | [URL](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac) | Thailand joined an explicit call for restraint, cessation of violence, humanitarian access, and civilian protection. This shows the program was translated into a formal multilateral stance with clear behavioral expectations.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`

- **`Thailand monitored Myanmar situation closely`** | **Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand** | **2024-04-19** | [URL](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/weeklypressbriefing190424-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | The government said it created a special committee and stayed open to dialogue with stakeholders. This is direct evidence of an institutional response mechanism rather than pure rhetorical positioning.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`

- **`Thailand’s official 2024 IAEA statement`** | **Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand** | **2024-09-26** | [URL](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/iaea-09162024-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Thailand emphasized safe and peaceful nuclear technology and strengthening nuclear safety, security, and safeguards. This is a narrower but real example of translating policy into institutional and safeguards language.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`

- **`Thailand ratified the disappearance treaty`** | **Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand** | **2024-05-16** | [URL](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/icpped140524-2?page=5d5bd3da15e39c306002aaf9) | Ratification of the disappearance convention and the accompanying anti-torture / anti-disappearance law is the clearest institutional and enforcement-related reform I found in 2024. It shows direct translation of rights rhetoric into legal machinery.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `7B.10`

- **`Victory: same-sex marriage in Thailand`** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-06-18** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/18/victory-same-sex-marriage-thailand) | Same-sex marriage passed under Srettha’s government. This is concrete legislative translation of a stated rights program into durable law.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`

- **`Thailand's Senate approved same-sex marriage bill`** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-06-18** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/18/victory-same-sex-marriage-thailand) | The final Senate approval strengthened the durability of the reform, showing the program was carried through an institutional process rather than left at the level of rhetoric.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`

- **`Srettha and his wife worth B1bn`** | **Bangkok Post** | **2024-06-17** | [URL](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2812379/declaration) | Public asset declaration to the anti-corruption commission is a small but real transparency step. It is not a full enforcement system, but it does show an institutionalized disclosure mechanism.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `7B.10`

**Negative / Mixed Evidence**
- **`Thai central bank holds key rate, defies government calls for cuts`** | **Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-04-10** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-central-bank-holds-key-rate-defies-government-calls-for-cuts-3372713) | The government pressed the independent central bank to cut rates, which shows that the economic program was not fully translated into a disciplined, institution-respecting framework. The plan existed, but the governance structure around it was contested.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`

- **`Forty Thai senators seek PM's dismissal over cabinet appointment`** | **Reuters via ThePrint** | **2024-05-17** | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/forty-thai-senators-seek-pms-dismissal-over-cabinet-appointment/2089532/) | The Pichit Chuenban appointment shows that some appointments were politically connected and ethically risky. This undercuts any claim that the governing program was translated only through clean technocratic or institution-centered choices.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- **`Thai court says PM Srettha violated rules on ethics in cabinet appointment`** | **Reuters via ThePrint** | **2024-08-14** | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/thai-court-says-pm-srettha-violated-rules-on-ethics-in-cabinet-appointment/2222960/) | The ethics ruling confirms that one of the central appointments driving the administration was not cleanly separated from conflict-of-interest concerns. That weakens the case for robust institutionalization of the broader program.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`, `7B.9`

- **`Thailand's 14 billion handout` and later coverage** | **Reuters via Yahoo News** | **2024-08-01** | [URL](https://www.yahoo.com/news/thailands-flagship-14-billion-handout-072635149.html) | Implementation snags and expert criticism show that Srettha’s flagship program had not yet become a stable delivery system. The priority was clear, but the enforcement and administrative pipeline were still weak.  
  **IDs:** `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`

**Search Gap**
- I did **not** find a standalone 2024 budget document, line-item spending plan, or enforcement manual that clearly links Srettha’s program to explicit budget allocations and implementation metrics.
- The evidence base is strongest on:
  - cabinet decisions
  - appointments
  - official foreign-policy positions
  - institutional/legal reforms
- It is weaker on:
  - formal budget architecture
  - internal enforcement memos
  - systematic implementation scorecards

**Bottom line:** Srettha did translate parts of his program into concrete measures, especially the digital-wallet plan, technocratic finance staffing, FTA and investment outreach, Myanmar crisis management, and a few legal reforms. The translation was real, but uneven and often incomplete.
